idiom_name: plain service class/function + ORM unit-of-work context manager
implementation_notes: The service is a plain class or module function whose collaborators are injected through the constructor (or a framework dependency such as FastAPI Depends); the unit of work is the ORM's own context manager - SQLAlchemy's sessionmaker.begin() / session.begin() opens the transaction, commits on clean exit and rolls back on exception, and Django's transaction.atomic does the same for the Django ORM. What replaces the classic structure is Python's with-block: the boundary is a lexical scope rather than an object the service owns, and the service never calls commit itself. A hand-written unit-of-work class holding the repositories is still justified when several repositories must share one session behind an explicit port for tests.
pitfalls: SQLAlchemy's autobegin starts a transaction on first use, so a forgotten session scope silently spans many operations.
A Session is not thread-safe or task-safe: one per thread/task (scoped_session, async_scoped_session), never a module-level shared session.
Django's ATOMIC_REQUESTS plus a service-level atomic() only creates a savepoint; a caught exception can leave the outer transaction dirty unless the service wraps the whole use case.
